en: Now, the Rāmāṣṭaka (The Eight Verses on Rāma).
I perpetually bow to Śrī Rāmacandra—the supreme friend of Sugrīva, the most purifying, whose body is like a fresh cloud, the recipient of compassion, and whose eyes are like lotuses. || 1 ||

I perpetually bow to Śrī Rāmacandra, the essence of saṃsāra, the ultimate teaching, the way of conduct, the descent of Dharma, the one who has destroyed the burden of the earth, who is eternally changeless, and the essence of the ocean of bliss. 2.

I perpetually bow to Śrī Rāmacandra, the playground of Lakṣmī, the abode of the worlds, the dwelling place of the gods on earth, the laughter of the ocean of bliss, the destroyer of Laṅkā, and the radiant palace.

I perpetually bow to Śrī Rāmacandra, who wears a garland of *mandāra* flowers, whose speech is as sweet as the *rasāla* fruit, whose virtues are vast, who struck down the seven *tāla* trees, who is a time of destruction for the flesh-eaters, and who is the protector of the world of the gods. || 4 ||

I perpetually bow to Śrī Rāmacandra, the knower of Vedānta, the destroyer of the pride of all beings, the foremost among the gods, the protector of Gajendra, and the one who is free from worldly expansion. || 5 ||
I constantly bow to Śrī Rāmacandra, who is fearless in play, who purifies his own kin, who is ever-singing, who is not harmed by words, and who is not captivated by passion in speech. || 6 ||

I perpetually bow to Śrī Rāmacandra, whose body is his divine play, who is steadfast on the stage of battle, the sole hero of the universe, the sustainer of Raghu’s lineage, whose roar is profound, and who has conquered all disputations. || 7 ||

I perpetually bow to Śrī Rāmacandra, who is delightful in his dark complexion, delightful to the eyes, delightful in his virtues, and delightful in his speech; he who is saluted by the entire world and whose devotion is the object of desire. || 8 ||
Thus ends the Rāmāṣṭaka in its entirety.
